items.rationale: The failed indoor heating-pipe joint is consistent with a local fracture under §2.4.3, even without a full burst. Four like-for-like repair elbows under §7.1.7(c) price at €42 gross.
Under §§7.1.5 and 7.1.8(e), a second set of four same-size elbows is not supported by the documented short repair. If separately substantiated, the set would price at €42 gross.
Case 40 supports €104 gross for five standard repair elbows under §7.1.7(c). The short repair description does not independently confirm all five, so attribution remains subject to §7.1.8(e).
Five additional 45° elbows are not supported by the localized repair under §7.1.8(e); the comparable repair lists just one such elbow. If documented, all five would price at €103 gross.
One standard elbow matches the fitting count in Case 40 and is allowable under §7.1.7(c) if used in the reconnection. The comparable gross allowance is €21.
Necessary repair fasteners are covered under §7.1.7(c). Eight screws price at €9.30 gross on the reference evidence.
Four clamps price at €19.20 gross, consistent with Case 43. They qualify under §7.1.7(c) only if used for this repair, and the stated 10 mm size is not confirmed by the description.
Clamps sized to the listed 15 mm pipe are ordinary repair fixings under §7.1.7(c), if fitted to the affected run. Four at approximately €5.25 gross each give €21.
Necessary plumbing labour is covered at customary rates under §7.1.7(g). The reference allowance for 6.75 hours is €619 gross.
The description confirms a helper for part of the job, so §7.1.7(g) supports this labour. The reference allowance for 5.75 hours is €409 gross.

Like-for-like pipe is covered under §7.1.7(c), but the reported one-metre cutout leaves the invoiced 6.4 m unsubstantiated under §7.1.8(e). If the full quantity is shown necessary, the reference allowance is €99 gross.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows the first travel charge for this contractor's repair invoice. The reference allowance is €80 gross.
Repair-specific installation consumables are covered under §7.1.7(c) provided they are not already itemised elsewhere. The reference flat-rate allowance is €43 gross.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes separate administrative and processing charges. The €15 gross figure is a nominal conditional estimate, not a payable allowance.

Like-for-like rock wool is covered under §7.1.7(c), but the full six metres need support under §7.1.8(e) given the reported short cutout. If required for reinstatement, the reference allowance is €135 gross.

The records do not show a separate need for six mats in addition to the pipe insulation, so §§7.1.8(c) and 7.1.8(e) weigh against payment. If separately justified, six ordinary mats at about €14 each give €84 gross.
Wire used to fasten the replacement insulation is a covered installation consumable under §7.1.7(c). Two units price at €26 gross on the reference evidence.

The two technician entries total 13.75 hours, broadly consistent with the reported day and a half, so this is not inherently a duplicate under §7.1.8(c). Seven covered repair hours under §7.1.7(g) price at €642 gross, excluding any time attributable solely to noncovered cleaning.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows only the first travel charge for this contractor on this invoice. €80 gross is the ordinary single-charge benchmark, not a second allowance.
Contractor protective equipment is excluded under §7.1.8(b), and the bundled set does not identify a separate covered repair consumable. €18 gross is a conditional estimate only.
Disposal of removed pipe and insulation is covered under §§5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a). The close plumbing references support €60 gross for one disposal charge.

Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.8(a) do not cover general hygiene work or coating without documented damage requiring it. If necessary removal of leak residue can be separated from the bundled work, allow about €50 gross for that limited cleanup, consistent with Case 18.
